of a competitor (or an affiliate of a competitor) of the Company. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">In addition to the criteria set forth above, and any others the Nominating and

practice 2.1.8 of the DCGC, including that an independent director must be free of any relationships which, in the opinion of the Board, would interfere with the exercise of independent judgment in carrying out the responsibilities of a director.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">As needed, the Nominating and Governance Committee may identify new potential director nominees by, among other means, requesting current directors and executive
officers and external advisors to notify it if they become aware of persons meeting the criteria described above who would be suitable candidates for service on the Board. The committee also may, as needed, engage one or more firms that specialize
in identifying director candidates. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">As appropriate, the Nominating and Governance Committee will review publicly available information regarding a potential
candidate, request information from the candidate, review the candidate&#146;s experience and qualifications, including in light of any other candidates the committee might be considering, and conduct, together with other members of the Board, one
or more interviews with the candidate. Committee members or their designees also may contact one or more references provided by the candidate or may contact other members of the business community or persons who may have first-hand knowledge of the
candidate&#146;s talents and experience. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14.5pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><A NAME="toc73007_29"></A>Diversity </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Board is committed to supporting, valuing and leveraging diversity, including gender and ethnic/cultural diversity, in its composition, among other qualities that
the Board believes serve the best interests of the Company and its stakeholders. As part of these efforts, the Board, while taking into account the overall profile and selection criteria for appointments of suitable candidates, has proposed a slate
of nominees to the Board in which at least 30% of director nominees are women and that includes a director nominee from an underrepresented ethnic group. The Board aims to continue in its efforts to have a diverse gender and ethnic composition as it
continues its board refreshment process. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14.5pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><A NAME="toc73007_30"></A>Board Refreshment </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Board, with the support of the Nominating and Governance Committee, maintains an orderly, robust process for Board refreshment and succession that is aimed at
maintaining an appropriate balance with respect to the expertise, experience and diversity on the Board. The Board and its Nominating and Governance Committee regularly evaluates the Board composition with respect to, among other matters, director
independence, skills, experience, expertise, diversity and other factors to ensure the Board remains well-qualified to provide effective oversight of the Company and management. The Board and the Nominating and Governance Committee regularly
consider the Company&#146;s strategy, performance, operations, relevant industry and market conditions, and current and anticipated needs in terms of particular areas of experience and expertise (e.g., risk oversight, industry, science), among many
other factors, to inform these refreshment practices. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">HOW OUR DIRECTORS ARE SELECTED AND EVALUATED (continued) </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Board continues its orderly Board succession and refreshment process, refreshing eight director seats since the
beginning of 2015. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Board also remains focused on committee composition and refreshment. In August 2018, the Board refreshed the chairs of the then two Board
committees (the Audit Committee and the Nominating and Compensation Committee) and, following the installment of the Nominating and Governance Committee in September 2019, the Board refreshed the composition of all three committees. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><A NAME="toc73007_31"></A>CERTAIN RELATIONSHIPS AND RELATED TRANSACTIONS </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Under the Rules of Procedure, a conflict of interest must be reported to the Board and the Board shall determine the consequences of such conflict, if any. In case of a
conflict of interest, the director concerned is not allowed to participate in discussions or vote on such matter. If all directors have a conflict of interest, the resolution concerned will be voted on by shareholders at the general meeting of
shareholders. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Other than the compensation items described below, no decisions to enter into material transactions in which there were conflicts of interest with
directors occurred during the financial year 2020. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="center"><B>34 </B></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><A NAME="toc73007_32"></A>HOW OUR DIRECTORS ARE COMPENSATED </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14.5pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><A NAME="toc73007_33"></A><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-Employee</FONT> Director Compensation for 2020 </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Compensation Committee has responsibility for reviewing and considering any revisions to compensation for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT>
directors. The Board reviews the Compensation Committee&#146;s recommendations and makes the final recommendation to the shareholders meeting regarding compensation for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> directors. Refer to Item 8
below for the board proposals to the Annual General Meeting to set the revised equity compensation to the Board. It is our policy to reimburse all directors for reasonable expenses incurred in performing their duties as a director. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B>Cash Compensation </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Sir Peter Bonfield, receives an
annual fixed fee of <FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman">&#128;</FONT>275,000 for serving as <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> director and chairman of the board. The other
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> directors receive an annual fixed fee of $85,000. In response to the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</FONT> pandemic, the nine <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT>
Directors proposed and accepted a 25&nbsp;percent reduction in their annual fixed fee effective April&nbsp;1, 2020 to December&nbsp;31, 2020. Members of the Audit Committee, Compensation Committee and Nominating and Governance Committee receive an
additional annual fixed fee of $15,000 and the chairs of each of these committees receive an additional annual fixed fee of $15,000. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B>Equity
Compensation </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">In 2020, each <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> director received an annual restricted share unit award with a grant
value of $200,000. The awards were granted at the same time as the NXP annual equity grants for NXP employees in October, and the restricted share units fully vest on the earlier of the first anniversary of the date of grant or the next annual
general meeting of shareholders. Unvested portions of their equity award are forfeited upon the termination of a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> director&#146;s service on the Board, except in the case of termination of service
upon death or at the request of the Board, in which case the unvested portion is fully accelerated. The annual grant value has been set at $200,000 since the initial public offering of the Company in August 2010. In Agenda item 8 it is proposed to
increase this annual equity grant value to $225,000. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B>Share Ownership Guidelines </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Members of our Board are subject to share ownership guidelines. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-executive</FONT> directors are prohibited from selling any shares of
the Company until they own shares that are valued at no less than five times the annual cash fixed fee paid to the director. Our executive director and President/CEO is subject to the share ownership guidelines described in Item 9 below. </P>

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><A NAME="toc73007_34"></A>ITEM 4: AUTHORIZATION OF THE BOARD TO ISSUE ORDINARY SHARES AND GRANT
RIGHTS TO ACQUIRE ORDINARY SHARES </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Board considers it in the best interest of the Company and its stakeholders for the Board to be able to react in a
timely manner when strategic business opportunities arise that require the issuance of ordinary shares. For example, this designation has been used in the past in relation to the issuance of convertible bonds in 2014. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">At the 2020 AGM, the shareholders authorized the Board to issue shares and to grant rights to acquire ordinary shares equal to 10% of the issued share capital for a
period of 18 months, effective from May&nbsp;27, 2020 until November&nbsp;27, 2021, and to exclude <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-emptive</FONT> rights in connection with such issue or grant of rights. It is proposed to renew this
authorization for a new period of 18 months, effective from May&nbsp;26, 2021 until November&nbsp;26, 2022, and up to 10% of the issued share capital. The Company&#146;s issued share capital as of March&nbsp;22, 2021<B> </B>was 289,519,638 ordinary
shares. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Although we presently do not have specific plans to issue ordinary shares for any purpose, the Board believes that it is advisable and in the best interest
of our shareholders for our shareholders to provide this general authorization in order to avoid the delay and expense of obtaining shareholder approval at a later date, and to provide us with greater flexibility to pursue financing opportunities,
such as the issuance of convertible notes, or acquisitions when market conditions are favorable. The issuance of a large number of ordinary shares could be dilutive to existing shareholders or reduce the trading price of our shares on Nasdaq. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Therefore, in accordance with standard Dutch practice, it is proposed to grant the Board the authorization to issue ordinary shares and grant rights to acquire ordinary
shares (up to 10% of the issued share capital) within the limits provided in the Articles of Association, which authorization can be used for general purposes. If this proposal is approved the prior authorization (from the 2020 AGM) will immediately
expire. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B>THE BOARD RECOMMENDS A VOTE &#147;FOR&#148; THE PROPOSAL TO AUTHORIZE THE BOARD TO ISSUE ORDINARY SHARES AND GRANT RIGHTS TO
ACQUIRE ORDINARY SHARES. </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><A NAME="toc73007_35"></A>ITEM 5: AUTHORIZATION OF THE BOARD TO RESTRICT OR EXCLUDE <FONT

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><A NAME="toc73007_36"></A>ITEM 6: AUTHORIZATION OF THE BOARD TO REPURCHASE ORDINARY SHARES OF
THE COMPANY </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">At the 2020 AGM, shareholders authorized the Board to acquire ordinary shares in the Company&#146;s capital for a period of 18 months. It is
proposed to renew this authorization for a period of 18 months from the Annual General Meeting, as set out below. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The purpose of this Item is to create flexibility
to return capital to the shareholders and to cover obligations of the Company to deliver ordinary shares. In addition to being a means to return value to shareholders, repurchases of shares of the Company&#146;s own share capital could be used by
the Board to demonstrate a commitment to the Company&#146;s business and confidence in the long-term growth of NXP, provide increased liquidity for investors and cover obligations under the Company&#146;s share-based compensation plans. Since 2017,
the Company has returned $8.175&nbsp;billion to shareholders through previously announced share repurchases and dividend payments, reducing our diluted share count by approximately 18&nbsp;percent, or 62&nbsp;million shares. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The number of ordinary shares to be repurchased, if any, and the timing and manner of any repurchases will be determined after taking into consideration, amongst other
things, prevailing market conditions and available resources. Under Dutch law, the number of shares held by the Company and its subsidiaries may not exceed 50% of the issued share capital. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">As of March&nbsp;22, 2021 the Company holds 13,772,811 treasury shares or 4.8 percent of the issued share capital. The Board considers it desirable to create the
flexibility to continue with share repurchases. As such, it is proposed to the shareholders to authorize the Board for a period of 18 months, with effect from the Annual General Meeting, to repurchase ordinary shares up to 10% of the issued share
capital as per the date of the Annual General Meeting. Shares may only be repurchased pursuant to this authorization so long as the total number of shares held by the Company in treasury does not exceed 20% of the Company&#146;s issued share
capital. The repurchases may take place on the open market, through privately negotiated repurchases, in self-tender offers, or through accelerated repurchase arrangements. Such repurchases may be made at prices ranging between <FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman">&#128;</FONT>0.01 and a price equal to 110% of the market price of the ordinary shares on Nasdaq, market price being the average of the closing prices for the ordinary shares on Nasdaq on the five trading days
prior to the date of the acquisition, provided that (i)&nbsp;for self-tender offers, the market price shall be the volume weighted average price (&#147;VWAP&#148;) for the ordinary shares on Nasdaq during a period, determined by the Board, of no
less than one trading day and no greater than five trading days prior to the expiration of the tender offer, and (ii)&nbsp;for accelerated repurchase arrangements, the market price shall be the VWAP for the ordinary shares on Nasdaq over the term of
the arrangement. If this authorization is granted, the existing authorization as granted in 2020 will cease to apply as per the moment this authorization takes effect. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B>THE BOARD RECOMMENDS A VOTE &#147;FOR&#148; THE PROPOSAL TO AUTHORIZE THE BOARD TO REPURCHASE THE COMPANY&#146;S ORDINARY SHARES.
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><A NAME="toc73007_37"></A>ITEM 7: AUTHORIZATION OF THE BOARD TO CANCEL THE COMPANY&#146;S ORDINARY SHARES HELD OR TO BE ACQUIRED
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">It is proposed to authorize the Board to cancel any or all ordinary shares in the share capital of the Company held or repurchased by the Company resulting
in a reduction of the Company&#146;s issued ordinary shares. The cancellation may be executed in one or more tranches. The number of ordinary shares that will be cancelled (whether or not in a tranche) will be determined by the Board, with a maximum
equal to the number of ordinary shares held or repurchased by the Company in its issued shared capital. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Pursuant to Dutch law, cancellation may not be effected
earlier than two months after the resolution to cancel ordinary shares is adopted and publicly announced; this will apply for each tranche. The purpose of this proposal is to authorize the cancellation of ordinary shares held by the Company or that
have been acquired in accordance with Item 6, to the extent that such ordinary shares shall not be used to cover obligations under share-based remuneration or other obligations. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B>THE BOARD RECOMMENDS A VOTE &#147;FOR&#148; THE PROPOSAL TO AUTHORIZE THE BOARD TO CANCEL THE COMPANY&#146;S ORDINARY SHARES HELD OR TO BE
ACQUIRED. </B></FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><A NAME="toc73007_38"></A>ITEM 8: APPROVAL OF THE AMENDED REMUNERATION OF THE <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">NON-EXECUTIVE</FONT> MEMBERS OF THE BOARD </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Compensation Committee has responsibility for reviewing and considering any
revisions to compensation for <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> directors, and in accordance with the Articles of Association any remuneration of the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> directors is subject to
the approval of the general meeting of shareholders. In addition to an annual fixed cash fee, which has remained unchanged since the initial public offering of the Company in August 2010, and cash compensation for members of Board committees set in
2020, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> directors receive an annual equity award. Equity awards are granted in the form of restricted share unit awards, and vest on the earlier of the first anniversary of the date of grant or the
next annual general meeting of shareholders. The maximum annual grant value has been set at $200,000, and has remained unchanged since the Company&#146;s IPO in August 2010. The Compensation Committee, advised by its independent advisor, has
compared the Board&#146;s remuneration with its peer group, and determined that the value of the NXP&#146;s <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> director pay package was below the Peer Group. In view thereof, considering the annual
equity grants to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> directors has been unchanged since the IPO in 2010, and in order to support the Board&#146;s ability to attract and retain talented
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> directors, the Board proposes to the Annual General Meeting to increase the annual equity grant value to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> directors from $200,000 to $225,000.
No further changes in cash remuneration to members of the Board are proposed. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B>THE BOARD RECOMMENDS A VOTE &#147;FOR&#148; THE AMENDED

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><A NAME="toc73007_42"></A>EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:14.5pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B><A NAME="toc73007_43"></A>Compensation Discussion&nbsp;&amp; Analysis </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">This Compensation Discussion and Analysis (&#147;CD&amp;A&#148;) describes our 2020 executive compensation program for the following executive officers (collectively,
the &#147;Named Executive Officers&#148; or &#147;NEOs&#148;): </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">We encourage shareholders to understand our beliefs in compensating and rewarding our NEOs. Therefore, we are providing an overview of
the philosophies, principles, and practices that we employ, as governed by the Board of Directors of NXP (the &#147;Board&#148;). The NEOs, under the leadership of our Executive Director and President and Chief Executive Officer (our
&#147;CEO&#148;) and the other members of the Board, are held accountable for delivering results, while simultaneously creating a culture of innovation and customer focus. The compensation of our CEO is determined by the Board in accordance with the
principles set forth in the remuneration policy for executive and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> directors previously approved by our general meeting of shareholders, as required under Dutch corporate law. Richard Clemmer
served as our Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer until his resignation from that position on May&nbsp;27, 2020, at which time Mr.&nbsp;Sievers was appointed as our Executive Director and President and Chief Executive Officer. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B>2020 No Ordinary Year </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">In 2020, the world
experienced a disruption never before seen with the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</FONT> pandemic. NXP, along with much of the semiconductor market, experienced a significant decline in revenue and production in the first half of the
year due to this unforeseen challenge. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Our first priority during this time was the safety and wellbeing of our employees, customers and suppliers. </B></P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">We enacted world-class health and safety protocols at all NXP sites and launched online information hub with NXP <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</FONT> policy information, frequently asked questions, guidance for working from home, ergonomic guidelines and access to wellness resources. </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">To keep our essential business running, more than half of our employee population continued working in our wafer fabs and
assembly and test sites. Additionally, engineers working in our high-security environments, employees needing access to labs and equipment, and those ensuring the
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">day-to-day</FONT></FONT> operations of NXP facilities also required access to our sites. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">We immediately supported many <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#147;non-essential&#148;</FONT> employees all over the world
to work from home during the multi-national quarantine. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">During those first few weeks, we concentrated on ensuring communication with our employees by appointing a project team
solely focused on coordinating policies and communications for the health and safety of our employees. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="3%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">Our remarkably resilient employee population saw little to no degradation of productivity even while the situation remained

impacting NXP proportionally more than some competitors. Despite this, NXP did not make any change to overall performance expectations for either short term or long-term incentives for our NEOs.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Our strong commitment to our pay for performance philosophy was reflected in the performance goals we established for 2020, and ultimately in the results and amounts
that were earned or vested under our annual and long-term incentive programs for our NEOs. We further detail these outcomes and our committed adherence to this philosophy for each pay component including at a high level: </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">At our annual general meeting of shareholders held on May&nbsp;27, 2020, we did not receive a majority of votes in favor of the proposal to approve, on a <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-binding,</FONT> advisory basis, our NEOs&#146; compensation. We recognized the importance of engaging our shareholders&#146; governance and investment stewardship teams to ensure that we understood their concerns on
this issue and our compensation program philosophy and design. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

meetings with the governance and investment stewardship teams of 25 of our largest shareholders, which represented approximately 59% of our identifiable and actively managed shares, to discuss specific concerns and solicit feedback regarding our
compensation programs and the publication of our proxy. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The feedback we received from our shareholders was direct and helpful. It included concerns regarding the magnitude of the equity incentive &#147;reboot&#148; grants in
2018 following the termination of the Qualcomm acquisition. We also heard concern about the terms of the advisory agreement with our former CEO taking effect in May 2020. These terms provided that he will serve as a strategic advisor to the Company
to ensure an effective transition of leadership and that he would receive continued vesting of certain of his equity awards through October&nbsp;31, 2021, subject to his continued service through that date. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION&nbsp;(continued) </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">We also discussed the design and payout ranges of our performance-based equity program. This program uses relative total
shareholder return as the performance measure over a three-year period. Target shares are earned if we are at the median of the identified and disclosed peer group of companies. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Shareholders with whom we connected generally provided positive feedback on our overall ongoing program design and found that we have an appropriate balance of short and
long-term rewards, with sufficient performance related elements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Ultimately, the key feedback we heard was that the magnitude of the 2018 awards was perceived
negatively while our overall ongoing program design was in line with market standards. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">In addition to specific comments on executive compensation, shareholders
expressed an interest in understanding important information about our workforce including demographics, diversity, equality and inclusion goals and statistics, how we invest in our current and future talent and how we monitor and manage retention.
We have included an explanation of these topics in the &#145;Human Capital Management&#146; section of this proxy statement beginning on page 5. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>What we did
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Our Board and executives thoughtfully considered and evaluated important information gathered from our shareholder engagement process and, together with feedback
and input from our independent compensation consultant, decided upon the most appropriate course of action considering all relevant stakeholders. Based on this process and the input we received from our shareholders, we believe our current ongoing
executive compensation program reflects current market practices and serves to strongly align the interests of our executives with those of our shareholders. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">We
acknowledge the shareholder concerns about the <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">one-time</FONT> &#147;reboot&#148; awards provided in the 2018. No grants of similar size have been made in 2019 and 2020, regardless of the extraordinary impact of
COVID, taking into consideration the feedback regarding the 2018 &#147;reboot&#148; grant. Mr.&nbsp;Clemmer, for his role as CEO through May 2020, was provided no new award in 2020 and his 2019 award represented 23% of the award provided in 2018.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">We structured Mr.&nbsp;Sievers&#146; compensation in connection with his promotion to CEO in 2020 with a focus on ensuring that his compensation is aligned with
market practices. Mr.&nbsp;Sievers received a promotional grant in July, according to the CEO Agreements entered into and disclosed in March 2020, upon taking the role of CEO and combined with his annual grant as CEO received a total award less than
the award provided as President in 2018. As CEO, his equity award was determined at 66% of the 2018 award granted as President. There is no current intention to provide exceptional awards to NEOs in the future. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">With respect to the performance-based equity program, the Compensation Committee of the Board (the &#147;Compensation Committee&#148; or the &#147;Committee&#148;)
considered the shareholder feedback and determined to continue with the current plan design. The Committee specifically considered that a common market practice is to have a single measure and have target payout at the median of the market, and
therefore no changes were warranted. Relative Total Shareholder Return (&#147;RTSR&#148;) is the prevailing measure among our peers for a three-year period which remains our ongoing measure for 2020 grants. It also represents the clearest connection
to shareholder interests. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">We have continued our standard practice of determining equity award sizes for all NEOs, including our new CEO, based on prevailing market
practice in our peer group. We are also maintaining the program elements that are discussed later with positive support from these shareholders. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Ongoing
Shareholder Engagement </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">We will continue a regular, proactive shareholder engagement approach with both the portfolio managers, sector equity analyst and
governance teams and including semi-annual outreach by our Chairman and other <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> directors to our top investors. We believe that regular engagement with our shareholders is important and will allow
us to continue to understand and respond to their feedback, questions, and concerns on a more real-time basis. Throughout this process, we will seek to gain feedback and answer questions on our business strategy, compensation practices, governance
topics, ESG and other related issues. Investor outreach has increased in 2020 focusing our efforts on virtually remaining connected. In those calls, investors have been given opportunity to ask questions and express ideas or concerns. In addition to
the Board engagement described above, management held discussions with 109 active shareholders representing 81% of our outstanding shares. Overall management held 275 unique investor meetings or events with existing and potential investors as well
as sell-side analysts. </P>

 </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B><A NAME="toc73007_44"></A>Compensation Philosophy </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">As previously described in the &#145;Corporate Governance&#146; section of this proxy statement, our long-term strategy is to maximize value for shareholders and other
stakeholders of the Company. By driving relative market share, exceeding customer expectations, as well as developing, rewarding and retaining a highly engaged workforce, we expect to be able to grow market share 50% faster than our peers. Our
purpose is to provide Secure Connections for a Smarter World, a mission inspired by our customer-focused passion to win. We have directly linked NEO pay to stakeholder interests including shareholders. This will be discussed in detail in following
sections of this CD&amp;A. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">We operate globally and our executives are located in multiple countries. As a result, our pay philosophy considers both the overall
importance of consistency across the geographies in which we operate and where our executive talent resides ensuring competitive practices within a local country. Our overarching pay strategy is to <B>Pay for Performance&#151;delivering highly
competitive overall pay for market leading performance.</B> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Our executive compensation program is designed to: </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B><A NAME="toc73007_45"></A>Key Practices in Determining Executive Compensation </B></FONT></P>

STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> Directors previously approved by our general meeting of shareholders, as required under Dutch corporate law. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The
compensation of our other NEOs is also governed by the Board with specific actions taken to ensure the direct connection of rewards to key performance outcomes aligning executive pay to short and long-term stakeholder interests. Overall, our
programs are competitive in the marketplace and highly incentive-based, with most of the compensation <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">at-risk</FONT> earned via our short- and long-term incentive programs based on overall Company and individual
performance. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

incentive plan payouts at 200% of target</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT
 COLOR="#0c5126"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#0c5126">&#10003;</FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8201;&#8202;Include a &#147;double-trigger&#148; provision under our cash and equity incentive plans in the event of a <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">change-in-control</FONT></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0c5126"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#0c5126">&#10003;</FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8201;&#8202;Maintain
 meaningful stock ownership guidelines for executives and Directors</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0c5126"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#0c5126">&#10003;</FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8201;&#8202;Use
an independent Compensation Consultant to guide the Compensation plans</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0c5126"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#0c5126">&#10003;</FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8201;&#8202;Evaluate
 competitive market practices to establish program design and targeted payout amounts</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0c5126"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#0c5126">&#10003;</FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8201;&#8202;Conduct
 an annual risk assessment of our compensation programs</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0c5126"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#0c5126">&#10003;</FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8201;&#8202;Maintain
 a robust claw back policy covering cash and equity incentive plan awards for executives and Directors</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0c5126"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#0c5126">&#10003;</FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8201;&#8202;Follow
 principles of our shareholder approved executive and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> director remuneration policy</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0c5126"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#0c5126">&#10003;</FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8201;&#8202;Conduct
 board-level outreach to shareholders to elicit feedback on our compensation program</P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top"></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" BGCOLOR="#f0f9ff">&nbsp;&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" BGCOLOR="#f0f9ff">
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B></B><FONT COLOR="#ff0072"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#ff0072"><I>&times;</I></FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8194;Provide
 for guaranteed salary increases or payouts for performance-based awards</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B></B><FONT COLOR="#ff0072"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#ff0072"><I>&times;</I></FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8194;Provide
 for excise tax <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">gross-ups</FONT> resulting from M&amp;A activity or terminations</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B></B><FONT COLOR="#ff0072"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#ff0072"><I>&times;</I></FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8194;Provide
 for excessive separation payments or liberal definitions of change in control, or single-trigger cash severance upon a change in control</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B></B><FONT COLOR="#ff0072"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#ff0072"><I>&times;</I></FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8194;Provide
 above market returns on deferred compensation plans</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B></B><FONT COLOR="#ff0072"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#ff0072"><I>&times;</I></FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8194;Permit
 short sales, hedging, and transactions involving derivatives of our stock</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B></B><FONT COLOR="#ff0072"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#ff0072"><I>&times;</I></FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8194;Provide
 personal loans, guarantees or other similar arrangements</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B></B><FONT COLOR="#ff0072"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#ff0072"><I>&times;</I></FONT></FONT>&#8195;&#8194;Allow
 the pledging of Company stock by directors, executive officers, and certain other employees</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:2.11em; text-indent:-2.11em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B></B><FONT COLOR="#ff0072"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman; " COLOR="#ff0072"><I>&times;</I></FONT></FONT><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">&#8195;&#8194;Re-price</FONT> or buyout options without shareholder approval</P></TD></TR>
</TABLE>

<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="center"><FONT COLOR="#ffffff"><B>Approach and Structure</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt" align="left">&nbsp;</P></TD>

<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e; padding-left:8pt"> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.56em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Base Salary</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.56em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>(see page
52)</B></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e"> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Provides a competitive fixed component of cash compensation</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Based on an individual&#146;s role, experience, capability, and
contributions</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Reviewed annually against competitive benchmarks in local
markets</P> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt">&nbsp;</P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-RIGHT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e; padding-right:2pt"> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Attracts, retains, motivates, and enables us to develop highly qualified
executive leaders</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;<B>Key Point:</B> because of COVID 19, fiscal 2020
salaries for our NEOs were voluntarily reduced by 25% from April&nbsp;1, 2020 through December&nbsp;31, 2020</P></TD></TR>
<TR BGCOLOR="#b8e5ff" STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e; padding-left:8pt"> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.56em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Annual Incentive Plan (&#147;AIP&#148;)</B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.56em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>(see page 53)</B></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e"> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Variable, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">at-risk</FONT> compensation</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Rewards achievement of business/function, and/or overall corporate results
against key Company near-term goals</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Performance measures and targets
evaluated annually and set by the Board</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Program focuses on Revenue growth
pertaining to market share and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</FONT> gross margin modified by individual performance</P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-RIGHT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e; padding-right:2pt"> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Rewards Company performance against challenging short-term targets, with highly
competitive rewards for outstanding performance</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;<B>Key Point: </B>2020
target bonuses were established for the NEOs based on their specific roles</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;<B>Key Point:</B> although short term performance against set financial targets
was impacted by unforeseen challenges; <B>no adjustments to those targets</B> were taken for the NEOs</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;<B>Key Point:</B> 2020 AIP did not fund in keeping with our pay for performance
philosophy</P> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt">&nbsp;</P></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt">
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e; padding-left:8pt"> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:0.56em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Performance-Based Restricted Stock Units (&#147;PSU&#148;)</B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:0.56em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>(see page 56)</B></P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-RIGHT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e"> <P STYLE="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Meaningfully incents management to execute on our longer-term business
objectives</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Drives long-term shareholder value creation</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Vesting based on <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">3-year</FONT> cliff vesting
using <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">3-year</FONT> RTSR measured against a defined Peer Group</P></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom" STYLE=" BORDER-LEFT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top" STYLE="BORDER-TOP:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-RIGHT:1px solid #21ff9e; BORDER-BOTTOM:1px solid #21ff9e; padding-right:2pt">
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Aligns with shareholder interests by driving superior performance against
longer-term corporate financial, operational, and strategic goals</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;Target
awards represent 70% of long-term incentive compensation value at time of award</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;<B>Key Point:</B> The Compensation Committee evaluated the PSU structure
considering shareholder feedback and a detailed review of practices within the NXP Peer Group</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; margin-left:1.78em; text-indent:-1.78em; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">&#149;</FONT>&#8195;&#8201;<B>Key Point:</B> PSUs granted in 2015, which have specific EBIT performance
targets of 10% per year compounded growth, were determined to have not met the performance criteria resulting in the cancellation of each such PSU, including those granted to our current and former CEOs, demonstrating our strong pay for performance
commitment. The target value forfeited by each of our former and current CEOs was $6.25M and $1.65M respectively valued at the time of grant. Value at the time of cancellation was $11.62M and $3.09M respectively considering stock price at time of
cancellation.</P></TD></TR></TABLE>

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>A Large Majority of Our NEOs&#146; Target Pay is <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">At-Risk</FONT> </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Our<B> performance-based culture and pay for performance philosophy</B> strongly align the interests of our NEOs with those of our stakeholders. As shown in the following
charts, our 2020 target executive compensation program was focused extensively on variable, performance-based and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">at-risk</FONT> compensation. Our current CEO, Mr.&nbsp;Sievers, has 92% of his target compensation at
risk with variable components. More than 60% is directly linked to performance of the company and himself. Our other executive officers who are NEOs, excluding our former CEO, also have 84% of their target compensation at risk. </P>

The average NEO figures include the annualized salary not impacted by the voluntary salary reduction and their target AIP percentage on average. The average NEOs exclude both our current and former CEO. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:18pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3">EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION&nbsp;(continued) </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">In addition to our Peer Group, the Compensation Committee, along with Mercer and management, reviews compensation
information from published surveys to assess select roles and provide a broader view of the local and global competitive marketplace. From time to time, we will evaluate information on pay levels and plan designs from other comparable companies that
we believe are important for a more comprehensive understanding of our industry and/or broader technology market practices. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">This market research is used to inform
program design principles along with the amount for each pay program and the overall total package. The Compensation Committee uses competitive benchmark data focusing on the median of the Peer Group to inform various compensation related decisions
including base salary, incentive targets and target equity award levels. While this benchmark information is used as a guideline, it is not used as a specific target. Other factors are also importantly considered in making final decisions for each
Pay Component such as experience, performance, role complexity, leadership capability, impact, etc. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">For 2020, the Compensation Committee&#151;in conjunction with
Mercer, the Compensation Committee&#146;s independent advisor, and management&#151;reviewed NXP&#146;s peer group (the &#147;Peer Group&#148;) for use in understanding market competitive pay levels for various executive positions, as well as other
competitive compensation practices and plan designs. To determine the companies to include in the Peer Group, a variety of factors were considered by the Compensation Committee, including revenue, market capitalization, enterprise value,
similarities to the industries in which we operate, and the overlapping labor market for top management talent. As a result of this review, the Compensation Committee made no changes to the Peer Group for 2020. The Compensation Committee reviews the
Peer Group regularly to ensure the most appropriate information is used in making executive compensation decisions. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">For 2020, our Peer Group consisted of the
following companies: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B><A NAME="toc73007_49"></A>2020 Compensation Decisions </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Considering the dramatic increase in responsibility and role for Mr.&nbsp;Sievers resulting from his promotion to CEO during 2020, the Compensation Committee evaluated
the full package that was appropriate for that new role. Each pay change will be described by element in the following pages, however, an overview of those changes and factors in the decision appear in the table below. Taking into consideration the
full package appropriate for the role of CEO, the Compensation Committee evaluated base salary, annual incentive target, long-term incentive targets, degree of performance related pay and their combined relevance to the competitive market. On target
with an annualized view, the total remuneration package was determined, outlined below, and is in line with CEO pay in the market. The full CEO package was described, and the overall increase is consistent with the typical increase in compensation
when an executive is promoted from president to CEO. This was also agreed upon and disclosed in the CEO Agreements in March 2020. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

incentive plan for the period January&nbsp;1, 2020 until May&nbsp;28, 2020. However, the performance targets for the first half were not achieved resulting in a 0% payout and forfeiture of the $833,812 target opportunity. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">For 2020, our AIP had two financial components weighted equally at 50% each. The overall payout opportunity is capped at 200% of target: </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B>Revenue Growth as Compared to Market: </B></FONT>NXP is a market leader in multiple markets.
Continuing to build on these leading positions, as well as expanding revenue and market share in other targeted markets, is vital to our continued success. Comparing to market is described below using the Total Available Market&#151;Focused (TAMF)
as defined by World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS). We also focus on profitable growth and therefore apply an additional requirement that Non-GAAP Operating Income must be greater than 31% of sales to achieve a revenue payout of greater than
100%. In 2019, Revenue Growth was also a performance measure but was determined with an annualized target growth percentage as opposed to being market relative. Any payout on this measure also depended upon maintaining and growing market share. The
cyclical nature of our industry prompted us to adjust this measure to being relative to market. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</FONT> Gross Margin Expansion:</B></FONT> <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</FONT> Gross Margin forms the cornerstone to driving our overall profitability. Successfully delivering differentiated new products that drive value to our customers is critical to driving profitable growth. This
is consistent with the measure used in 2019 representing continued focus on gross margin. </P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Because the semiconductor industry, especially in the
markets NXP serves, has historically cyclical performance, NXP developed performance targets for each half of the year in 2020 to be measured and judged independently for purposes of the Annual Incentive Plan payout. This differs from previous
approaches in that the performance targets were no longer based upon an annual view. The payout would continue to be made on an annual basis as the sum of the two half yearly measurements. Setting targets for each half year is reflective of the
nature of business performance and allows us to better align rewards to performance. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Although the Compensation Committee&#146;s decision to implement a relative
revenue growth metric and two semiannual measurements was made independently from the global <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19</FONT> pandemic, we believe these changes reflect best practices in the context of the pandemic. The sudden and
severe disruption to the global economy in the first half of 2020 created very different market conditions for us and many companies than in the second half of 2020. The relative nature of the revenue growth metric and the semiannual performance
periods enabled us to gauge performance under our 2020 AIP without having to make disruptive <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">mid-cycle</FONT> modifications. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Bonus

</TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT STYLE="font-family:ARIAL" COLOR="#0221d3"><B>NXP Revenue (AIP) Growth Compared to
Market</B></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:ARIAL">&nbsp;is measured as a factor of the market growth.&nbsp;If NXP grows at the same rate as the market (1.0x), the threshold is met and the measure will begin to fund. Our target is to grow 1.5x the
market.&nbsp;Market is measured as the Total Available Market&#151;Focused (TAMF) as defined by World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS). There is an additional requirement that 2020 Non-GAAP Operating Income be <FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman"><FONT STYLE="FONT-FAMILY:SYMBOL">&#179;</FONT></FONT> 31% of 2020 GAAP Revenue to payout the revenue component above 100%. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT STYLE="font-family:ARIAL" COLOR="#0221d3"><B><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</FONT> Gross Margin
Expansion</B></FONT><FONT STYLE="font-family:ARIAL">&nbsp;is measured as improving Non-GAAP Gross Margin over the previous year&#146;s performance. <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Non-GAAP</FONT> Gross Margin threshold was set at 53.0% for the
first half and 54.0% for the second half. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">NXP Revenue (AIP), Non-GAAP Operating Income, and Non-GAAP Gross Margin are non-GAAP financial measures. We
calculate NXP Revenue (AIP) by adjusting GAAP revenue to exclude the impact of acquisitions and divestitures and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-semiconductor</FONT> revenue. We calculate Non-GAAP Operating Income and Non-GAAP Gross Margin by
adjusting GAAP Operating Income and Gross Margin, respectively, to exclude the effects of purchase price accounting, restructuring, stock-based compensation, merger-related costs, and other incidentals. These measures should not be considered as a
substitute for, or superior to, the measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Clearly 2020 was significantly impacted by the COVID 19
pandemic. In the first half 2020, we saw dramatic market downturns. In keeping with our strong pay for performance philosophy, the measures that were <B>set forth at the beginning of the year were not adjusted for market conditions or the impact of <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">COVID-19.</FONT></B> Despite overcoming challenges and building a recovery trajectory, we will not payout short term incentives to our NEOs. We believe our NEOs are ultimately responsible for delivering results despite
economic and environmental conditions. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">Though our executives are responsible to overcome challenges and deliver performance, our Compensation Committee authorized a
second half Revenue Bonus Program that would allow for other <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-executive</FONT> AIP eligible employees, to earn a special bonus if we achieved a certain revenue target for the second half of 2020. The bonus was
intended to provide motivation and focus to return to delivering revenue growth, crucial to our recovery. The revenue target was achieved for the Revenue Bonus Program with target amounts being paid to eligible recipients. NEOs were ineligible for
this bonus, which was funded once we achieved a specified revenue target for second half, and will receive no payout. </P>
 <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="center"><B>55 </B></P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">A fundamental underpinning of our LTI program design is to align our NEOs&#146; and other key strategic decision makers&#146; interests with those of our shareholders.
The roles that our NEOs play are critical to NXP&#146;s long-term success, including driving our vision, strategy, and corporate culture. As a result, we tie 70% of our NEO&#146;s target LTI to NXP&#146;s relative stock price performance. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The number of shares awarded under the LTI program are determined by taking the target annual LTI award value and dividing it by the grant date closing price. For the
July&nbsp;28, 2020 promotional grant for Mr.&nbsp;Sievers, the grant date closing price was $115.24. For the annual LTI awards on October&nbsp;27, 2020, the grant date closing price was $133.23. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B><A NAME="toc73007_50"></A>Executive Share Ownership Guidelines </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">In addition to our strong <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pay-for-performance</FONT></FONT> philosophy and overall executive
compensation program design, we further align our executives&#146; interests with those of our shareholders through the NXP Executive Equity Ownership Policy (the &#147;EOP&#148;). The EOP applies to all NEOs as well as other senior executives of
the Company. All the NEOs are in compliance with their respective ownership guideline. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Claw back Policy </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">AIP payments and LTI grants are subject to the claw back
provisions mandated pursuant to Dutch corporate law. Under this provision, the Company is entitled to recover any performance-based compensation awarded in full or in part to the extent that such payment was made based on incorrect information
regarding the performance against <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-established</FONT> goals or about the circumstances from which the entitlement to the award was made dependent. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Derivatives Trading, Hedging, and Pledging Policies </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">NXP employees and directors are prohibited at all times from, either directly, or indirectly, purchasing financial instruments (including
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-paid</FONT> variable forward contracts, equity swaps, collars, and exchange funds), or otherwise engaging in transactions, that hedge or offset, or are designed to hedge or offset, any decrease in the market
value of NXP securities. No NXP employee or director may engage in hedging, pledging, hypothecating (including holding in margin accounts), or short selling NXP securities, or causing any other person to do so. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>Change of Control Policy </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Board believes that having a clear, consistent
policy that determines the appropriate treatment of our NEOs in the event of a change of control of the Company is in the best interest of NXP. This ensures our executives are able to fully focus on the potential transaction in the best interest of
the shareholders, without concern for their own disposition. The change of control benefits for our NEOs are described in the table and narrative under the &#147;Potential Payments Upon Termination of Change of Control Table&#148; section of this
proxy on page 69. All NEOs have a double-trigger provision such that, if they are involuntarily terminated without cause or leave with good reason (as defined in the applicable agreement) within 12 months following a change of control, they will

<P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B><A NAME="toc73007_54"></A>Compensation Practices and Risk </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Compensation Committee has oversight responsibility for evaluating risks related to the Company&#146;s compensation policies and practices. The Committee believes
our compensation programs balance an appropriate mix of short- and long-term performance objectives, cash- and equity-based compensation, and risks and rewards for our employees. Our programs incorporate key design features to mitigate the
likelihood of excessive risk-taking behavior, including: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

Company. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B><A NAME="toc73007_55"></A>Governance </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Compensation Committee oversees the compensation and benefits programs for our NEOs and is comprised solely of independent,
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</FONT> members of the Board. The Compensation Committee works very closely with its independent consultant and with management to examine the effectiveness of the Company&#146;s executive compensation
program throughout the year. The Compensation Committee Charter, which may be accessed at <U>http://investors.nxp.com</U>, details full authority and responsibility. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>The Role of the Compensation Committee </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Compensation Committee is
accountable for ensuring that the links between our executive compensation program and our business goals are responsible, appropriate, and strongly aligned with shareholders&#146; and other stakeholders&#146; interests. Under the responsibility of
and as assigned by the Board, the Compensation Committee annually establishes the compensation levels of our NEOs and reports to the full Board for their approval considering several factors, including: </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>The Role of the Independent Consultant </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">The Compensation Committee retained Mercer during 2020 to serve as its executive compensation consultant. Mercer provides advice directly to the Compensation Committee.
Other teams within Mercer and its affiliates perform services for us as described below. The individuals supporting the Compensation Committee did not perform any services for us other than as directed by the Compensation Committee. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">During fiscal 2020, Mercer advised the Compensation Committee on a variety of subjects such as compensation plan design and trends, pay for performance analytics,
external competitive compensation reference points, and other such matters. Mercer reports directly to the Compensation Committee, participates in meetings as requested and communicates with the Compensation Committee Chair between meetings, as
necessary. The Compensation Committee has the sole authority to: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL">As noted above, in 2020 other teams within Mercer or its affiliates provided services at the request of management to the Company not related to advising the
Compensation Committee on executive officer and director compensation matters.&nbsp;Fees paid to Mercer and its affiliates for services provided in 2020 related to executive and director compensation totaled approximately $330,000.&nbsp;Fees paid to
Mercer and its affiliates for actuarial valuations of pension plans and consulting services related to broad-based employee benefit plans totaled approximately $200,000.&nbsp;In addition, Mercer acts as the broker of record for broad-based employee
benefit plans in various countries in which we operate.&nbsp;As broker of record they received commissions directly from the benefit providers of approximately $940,000.&nbsp;In addition, in 2020, the Company paid Marsh, an affiliate of Mercer,
approximately $100,000 for fees related to insurance brokerage services unrelated to employee benefit programs and site services.&nbsp;Additionally, as part of its insurance brokerage services, Marsh receives insurance premium payments from the
Company which Marsh pays to insurance carriers on behalf of the Company. Because these other services were in the ordinary course of business, the Compensation Committee did not specifically approve such services, although the Compensation Committee
is aware of these other services. Mercer has safeguards and procedures in place to maintain independence in its executive compensation consulting practice. These safeguards include a rigidly enforced code of conduct, a policy against investing in
client organizations and separation between Mercer&#146;s executive compensation consulting and their other administrative and consulting business units from a leadership, performance measurement and compensation perspective.&nbsp;Specifically,
Mercer has adopted Global Business Standards for Executive Compensation to manage actual or perceived conflicts of interest and ensure the integrity of their advice.&nbsp;It addresses how they manage the executive compensation consulting
relationship, ensure the quality of consulting services and structure their business to prevent conflicts of interest. Mercer&#146;s executive compensation consultants are not managed or rewarded based upon client revenue from other lines of
business or other Marsh &amp; McClennan (MMR) companies other than to the extent all employees benefit from overall success of MMR.&nbsp;The Compensation Committee has assessed the independence of Mercer under NASDAQ listing standards and has
concluded that no conflict of interest exists. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:16pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><FONT COLOR="#0221d3"><B><A NAME="toc73007_56"></A>Compensation Committee Report </B></FONT></P>
